# One-way random-effects models

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Introduction to Random Effects and Mixed Models*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-05-25.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/Lecture15RandomEffectsMixedModels.pdf))
covers [fixed](#def-fixed-effect) versus [random effects](#def-random-effect),
[one-way random-effects ANOVA](#def-one-way-re),
variance components and their [method-of-moments estimates](#cor-mom-vc),
and [nested random effects](#def-nested-re)
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::

# Multilevel models: complete, no, and partial pooling

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Multilevel Models*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-05-27.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/Lecture16MultilevelModels.pdf))
covers complete, no, and [partial pooling](#thm-partial-pooling) of the Minnesota radon data,
random intercepts and slopes with `lmer()`,
and shrinkage
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
Richard McElreath's
[*Multilevel Models*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jh3RltVrQ-Q)
(Statistical Rethinking 2026, Lecture B01)
introduces multilevel models and partial pooling.
The lecture fits these models using [Bayesian inference](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-bayesian-paradigm);
the same model structures can also be fit by [maximum likelihood](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-mle),
as this chapter does with `lmer()`
[@mcelreath2026rethinking].
:::

{{< include _subfiles/intro-multilevel-models/_sec-pooling.qmd >}}

# Adding predictors to a multilevel model

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Multilevel Models II*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-06-01.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/Lecture17MultilevelModelsII.pdf))
covers adding county-level uranium as a group-level predictor for the radon data,
and multilevel [logistic regression](logistic-regression.qmd#def-logistic-regression) with `glmer()`
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
Richard McElreath's
[*Multilevel Model Expansion*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nv2rm1s9q6I)
(Statistical Rethinking 2026, Lecture B02)
continues Lecture B01's treatment of multilevel models,
again using [Bayesian inference](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-bayesian-paradigm)
[@mcelreath2026rethinking].
:::
